---
title: "Setup"
subtitle: "Ten minutes, before Day 1"
---

## 1. Open the setup notebook

All labs run in [Google Colab](https://colab.research.google.com/), so there is nothing to install. You need a Google account.

Open the setup notebook from the [notebooks page](notebooks.qmd) and choose **Runtime → Run all**. It checks the runtime and tells you which provider the API labs will use.

For the labs from Module 2 onward, switch on a GPU: **Runtime → Change runtime type → T4 GPU**. The free tier is enough for every lab.

## 2. Add API keys (optional)

Some labs call commercial APIs. Keys are optional: with none set, those labs run on a small open model from Hugging Face, and you can still complete every exercise.

If you have keys, add them to **Colab Secrets** (the key icon in the left sidebar), and switch on **Notebook access** for each:

| Secret name | Used in | Where to get a key |
|---|---|---|
| `{{< var secrets.openai >}}` | Modules 8, 11, 13–15 | [platform.openai.com](https://platform.openai.com/) |
| `{{< var secrets.anthropic >}}` | Modules 8, 11, 13–15 | [console.anthropic.com](https://console.anthropic.com/) |
| `{{< var secrets.typesafe >}}` | Modules 12–15 | [typesafe.ai](https://typesafe.ai/) |

::: {.callout-important appearance="simple"}
Never paste a key into a notebook cell. Colab Secrets keeps keys out of the notebook file, so they cannot be shared or committed by accident.
:::

Each API lab states its approximate cost for one full run.

::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple"}
Install TypeSafe's SDK only under its official name, `typesafe-sdk`; the labs install it for you. Several lookalike packages on PyPI, such as `typesafe-ai` and `jev`, are not published by TypeSafe.
:::

## 3. Check the prerequisites

The [home page](index.qmd#prerequisites) lists what the workshop assumes. If PyTorch is rusty, the official [60-minute blitz](https://pytorch.org/tutorials/beginner/deep_learning_60min_blitz.html) covers what you need.

## 4. Module 0 (optional)

[Module 0 · {{< var modules.m00.title >}}](lectures/00-coding-agents.qmd) is a self-serve hour, 08:00–09:00 on Day 1, or at home beforehand. Unlike the labs it runs on your own laptop, not in Colab: you install a terminal coding agent, git and the GitHub CLI, so you need permission to install software and a GitHub account. Its page walks you through the installs. Nothing later in the workshop depends on it.

## Coding assistants (optional)

If you want an AI coding agent in your terminal, [Coding assistants in the terminal](coding-assistants.qmd) shows how to install Codex, Claude Code, Gemini CLI or Kimi Code and gives each one a short, checkable task. None of them is needed for the labs.

## Running locally (optional)

Colab is the supported environment. To run the notebooks on your own machine, install [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) and run:

```bash
git clone {{< var repo.url >}}
cd {{< var repo.name >}}
uv run --group notebooks jupyter lab
```

Set the API keys as environment variables with the same names as the secrets above.
